description: VYBER transactions are treated as debits, so their amount is negated like VYDAJ and they enter the signed-amount average.

c.request: Linking each transaction to its account (skipping transactions without one), for each account statement frequency work out the average signed transaction amount — credits ('PRIJEM') positive, withdrawals negative, and any transaction that is neither left out — along with the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep the frequencies above it, and give me one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean. Don't round. VYBER transactions are treated as debits, so their amount is negated like VYDAJ and they enter the signed-amount average.
c.sql:
WITH per_frequency AS (
    SELECT
        a.frequency,
        AVG(CASE
                WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                WHEN t.type IN ('VYDAJ', 'VYBER') THEN -t.amount
            END) AS avg_signed_amount,
        AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    WHERE t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ', 'VYBER')
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
mean_signed AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_avg_signed_amount
    FROM per_frequency
)
SELECT
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount) AS avg_signed_amount,
    AVG(p.avg_balance) AS avg_balance,
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount - m.mean_avg_signed_amount) AS avg_excess_signed_amount
FROM per_frequency AS p
CROSS JOIN mean_signed AS m
WHERE p.avg_signed_amount > m.mean_avg_signed_amount;

b.request: Join each transaction to its account, excluding transactions without a matching account; for each account statement frequency, calculate the average signed amount for all transactions, counting PRIJEM as positive and VYDAJ and VYBER as negative while excluding other transaction types, and the average post-transaction balance. Compute the simple mean of the per-frequency signed-amount averages, retain frequencies whose signed-amount average is above that mean, and return one row with the averages of their signed-amount averages, balance averages, and excesses over the mean, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH per_frequency AS (
    SELECT a.frequency,
           AVG(CASE
                   WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                   WHEN t.type IN ('VYDAJ', 'VYBER') THEN -t.amount
               END) AS avg_signed_amount,
           AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
mean_signed_amount AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_avg_signed_amount
    FROM per_frequency
)
SELECT AVG(p.avg_signed_amount) AS avg_signed_amount_average,
       AVG(p.avg_balance) AS avg_balance_average,
       AVG(p.avg_signed_amount - m.mean_avg_signed_amount) AS avg_excess_over_mean
FROM per_frequency AS p
CROSS JOIN mean_signed_amount AS m
WHERE p.avg_signed_amount > m.mean_avg_signed_amount;

a.request: Joining each transaction to its account (dropping transactions with no matching account), compute for each account statement frequency (`account.frequency`) the average signed transaction amount — `trans.amount` taken as positive when `trans.type` is 'PRIJEM', negative when it is 'VYDAJ' or 'VYBER' (treating 'VYBER' as a debit), and left out (no value) for every other type — and the average `trans.balance` over all its transactions. Then take the plain mean of those per-frequency average signed amounts, keep only the frequencies whose average signed amount is above that mean, and return a single row with: the average of their average signed amounts, the average of their average balances, and the average of how far their average signed amount exceeds the mean. Don't round.
a.sql:
WITH account_averages AS (
    SELECT
        a.frequency,
        AVG(CASE
                WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                WHEN t.type IN ('VYDAJ', 'VYBER') THEN -t.amount
            END) AS avg_signed_amount,
        AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
frequency_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_signed_amount
    FROM account_averages
)
SELECT
    AVG(aa.avg_signed_amount) AS avg_of_above_mean_signed_amounts,
    AVG(aa.avg_balance) AS avg_balance_for_above_mean_frequencies,
    AVG(aa.avg_signed_amount - fm.mean_signed_amount) AS avg_excess_above_mean
FROM account_averages AS aa
CROSS JOIN frequency_mean AS fm
WHERE aa.avg_signed_amount > fm.mean_signed_amount;

d.request: For each account statement frequency, treat VYBER transactions as debits by negating their amounts, just like VYDAJ transactions, and include them in the signed-amount average.
d.sql: SELECT a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type IN ('VYDAJ', 'VYBER') THEN -t.amount ELSE t.amount END) AS average_signed_amount FROM account AS a JOIN trans AS t ON t.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.frequency;
